pages.text: You can create your own Music Disc on a workbench or using the $(6)Create$() add-on.
pages.title: Blank Music Disk

pages.text: Next, you need to create a label with which you can change the name and author of the Music Disc.

pages.title: Music Label
pages.text: To change the name and author, select Music Label in the quick access slot and press the RMB. Each time a Music Disc is created, it is not necessary to change its label.

pages.title: Etching table
pages.text: We've already made a Music Disc and a label for it. Now let's put them together for $(9)on etching table$().

Going into it, we will see at the top a field for a URL link, a plate with a Music Label and a menu with a selection of the core of the plate. The most important part in all this is the URL link.$(br2)To get a link to a track, you need to go to the website with the music and select the track you like,

click on the download button of the PC and select $(l)Copy the link address $().$(br2)All your songs are saved in the $(n)cache$(), in the etched-sounds folder, at the root of the build. Thanks to this, you don't have to worry about permanent and temporary links.

Trusted sites from which it is best to take links (but this does not mean that it is impossible from others): $(br)$(l:https://rus.hitmotop.com)Hitmo$() $(br)$(l:https://www.newgrounds.com/audio)Featured Audio$() $(br)$(l:https://ru.drivemusic.me)DriveMusic$() $(br)$(l:https://mus.zvukofon.com)MusPortal$() $(br)$(l:https://mp3uks.ru)mp3uks$() $(br2)Only mp3/wav/ogg are supported. YouTube and any cloud storage are not supported.

After all this process, select the core of the Music Disc you like and take it away.$(br)The name of the newly created Music Disc can be changed to $(9)anvil$().$(br2)Music $(n)everywhere$() will be played in a loop, except for $(9)Jukebox$().
